overview: Togo's women's health story is driven by government public-health programmes rather than a private femtech sector. The standout is Wezou, a national free-maternal-care scheme launched in 2021 that enrols pregnant women on a digital platform via health-worker smartphones, alongside a Ministry-led national digital health strategy and an HPV vaccine rollout begun in December 2023. Maternal mortality remains high and modern contraceptive use low, with family planning still largely donor-funded. There is no visible venture-backed femtech startup scene; instead, women-in-tech activity centres on state and donor training programmes such as NanaTech.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity is dominated by public-health milestones: the HPV vaccine introduction, published evidence on a rural obstetric ambulance service, and government reporting on the Wezou maternal programme.

items.text: Togo introduced the HPV vaccine into routine immunisation on 4 December 2023 to prevent cervical cancer, supported by Gavi, WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA and the Togolese Red Cross.

A Journal of Global Health study found a free rural ambulance service in four Northern Togo districts, run with Integrate Health, raised coverage of complicated obstetric cases from 18% (2020) to 66.5% (2022).
Government reporting put the Wezou maternal programme at over 1.3 billion CFA spent and roughly 200,000 beneficiaries at that reporting point, part of a total of about 400,640 women enrolled.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Togo's women's health policy runs through national programmes for free maternal care, a family planning scale-up plan, and a national digital health strategy under the 2023-2027 health development plan.

items.text: The Ministry of Health launched Wezou ("breath of life" in Kabye), a national programme removing the cost of essential maternal and newborn care and enrolling women on a digital platform via health-worker smartphones.

A government subsidy was introduced to cover 50% of contraceptive needs, with national family planning contributions set to rise 25% annually through 2026, though donors still fund over 80% of FP resources.
UNFPA's Togo Country Programme Document 2024-2026 sets targets to raise modern contraceptive prevalence and reduce unmet need for family planning.

Since 2021 the Fondation Pierre Fabre has helped the Ministry of Health build a National Digital Health Center (CNSD) and eHealth strategy, with early focus on teledermatology and maternal-infant tele-ultrasound.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Health-tech and women-in-tech activity is led by government and donor programmes rather than startups: the Wezou digital platform, community-health-worker obstetric referral, and the NanaTech women's digital programme.

items.text: On the Wezou digital platform, a midwife or nurse enrols each pregnant woman by smartphone and assigns an ID used through pregnancy and childbirth; antenatal follow-up in one district rose from 86.1% (2020) to 99.5% (2023).

Integrate Health's community health workers screen women for obstetric danger signs and trigger a free ambulance, transporting 2,926 pregnant and postpartum women across four Northern districts in the study period.
NanaTech Entrepreneures, part of the Ministry of Digital Economy's NanaTech programme, closed its first six-month cohort with a Demo Day in Lome where 45 women pitched projects to investors.

A national workshop at the University of Lome (August 2025) organised by Agence Togo Digital with GIZ ProDigiT support brought about 60 participants from Lome, Kara and Sokode to boost women's participation in tech.

sections.heading: Key players & programmes
sections.narrative: The visible actors are government programmes, an NGO and international agencies rather than commercial femtech companies.

items.name: Wezou (Ministry of Health)
items.note: National free-maternal-care programme with a digital enrolment platform; ~400,640 women enrolled and ~221,802 deliveries covered by 2024 reporting.

items.name: Integrate Health
items.note: Runs an integrated primary-care and free rural ambulance model with the Ministry of Health, lifting complicated-obstetric-case coverage to 66.5% in Northern Togo.

items.name: National Digital Health Center (CNSD)
items.note: Ministry of Health eHealth reference centre built with the Fondation Pierre Fabre; early services include maternal-infant tele-ultrasound and teledermatology.

items.name: NanaTech Entrepreneures
items.note: Ministry of Digital Economy programme training women entrepreneurs in digital tools and e-commerce; first cohort of 45 women completed in Lome.

items.name: UNFPA Togo
items.note: Supports family planning supplies and SRH under the 2024-2026 country programme; funds a large share of contraceptive commodities.

items.name: Gavi / HPV programme
items.note: Backed the December 2023 HPV vaccine introduction and 2023 catch-up campaign for girls aged 9-14, against cervical cancer.

sections.heading: Notable funding & investment
sections.narrative: Funding is public and donor-driven, flowing to government maternal-health and family-planning programmes rather than to companies.

items.purpose: Fund free essential maternal and newborn care for all pregnant women through the digital enrolment platform.
Subsidise contraceptive commodities, with national contributions planned to rise 25% annually through 2026.
Introduce HPV vaccine into routine immunisation and run the catch-up campaign for girls aged 9-14.

sections.heading: Active funders & partners
sections.narrative: The financing base is international agencies and foundations working through the Togolese state; there is no dedicated Togo gender-lens venture capital.

items.name: UNFPA
items.role: Funds family planning supplies and SRH programming under the Togo 2024-2026 country programme.

items.name: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance
items.role: Financed and supported the HPV vaccine introduction and catch-up campaign against cervical cancer.

items.name: Fondation Pierre Fabre
items.role: Technical and financial partner building Togo's National Digital Health Center and eHealth strategy.

items.name: Integrate Health
items.role: Implements and studies the integrated primary-care and free obstetric ambulance model with the Ministry of Health.

items.name: GIZ (ProDigiT)
items.role: Supports women-in-tech capacity building through Agence Togo Digital workshops.

sections.heading: White papers & reports
sections.narrative: Evidence comes from UN agencies, peer-reviewed studies and government-adjacent policy analyses; note that human rights reporting has documented serious maternal care gaps.

items.text: Regional Disparities in HPV Vaccination Coverage Among Girls Aged 9-14 in Togo (Vaccines, 2025): coverage of 46.5%, ranging from 76% in Kara to 15% in Grand Lome.
Analysis of the Political Economy and Financing of Family Planning in Togo: modern contraceptive prevalence rose from 17.1% (2014) to 23.2% (2023); donors fund over 80% of FP resources.
UNFPA Togo Country Programme Document 2024-2026 with family planning and SRH targets.
Amnesty International (2023): documented staff shortages and poor facilities, with some women giving birth on the floor.
